author: Mark Atwood
text:
Closed 2026-05-13 (Path B-wide-C — parameterized hex, no new deps).

Decision recap:
  * Original framing said 'Path A is fine, demo-only'. Investigation found chat spec normatively mandates ULIDs (line 430: 'All Chat IDs are ULIDs') and uses lex-ordering for unreadCount semantic (line 486).
  * Investigation also found jmap-mail-server already mints lex-orderable 16-char hex via timestamp+counter at email.rs:1748 — so the canonical doesn't need to change.
  * Mark chose B-wide-C: keep the 3-arg signature, change format from '<type><n>' to '<type><n:016x>'. Zero new deps. Cookie-cutter aligned.

Implementation:
  * Single mechanical edit in 6 *-server MemoryBackend impls: chat, calendars, contacts, metadata, sharing, tasks.
  * Doc-comments unified across the 6 siblings (previously varied terse vs. multi-line).
  * jmap-mail-server untouched per workspace canonical-template rule.
  * Test sweep zero-impact (none of the workspace tests assert literal next_id output).
  * cargo test --workspace, clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, fmt --all --check all pass.
  * Committed as 501c04f.

Future ULID work (if it's ever wanted):
  * Production backends already mint their own ids (not via this helper) — no work needed.
  * If a contributor wants to swap the demo MemoryBackends to real ULIDs, the format-string is now the only line that changes.
